title: Production main loop reuses test-seam runOnePollCycle which never submits triggers
description: runOnePollCycle is documented as the T-009 test seam and explicitly skips trigger submission with the comment 'In runOnePollCycle (test seam), we skip submission'. The production main() loop then calls the same runOnePollCycle for every tick with no separate signing/submitting path. As a result, the keeper's main loop logs trigger_attempt but NEVER calls signAndSubmitTrigger, never invokes the Ed25519 keypair generated at boot, and never emits a trigger_fired line. The whole purpose of the keeper is unwired in production.
impact: AC3.10 (keeper builds AND submits the trigger transaction signed with the ephemeral key) is unsatisfied at runtime. AC3.12 keeper-side prerequisite (trigger_fired log line, owner-routed output) cannot be observed. This is exactly the Cycle 1 'structural fix that doesn't actually wire through' regression class the contract calls out under Implementation guidance. Tests pass because T-009 only asserts on the discovery+price half and the trigger evaluation produces logTriggerAttempt without further wiring.
recommendation: Split into two functions: runOnePollCycleReadOnly (what currently exists, used by T-009) and runOnePollCycleWithSubmitter (accepts a signer + signAndSubmit dependency, called by main). Production must build, sign, submit, and call logTriggerFired/logTriggerFailed, then call registry.markTriggered.
evidence:
// Note: trigger submission requires a signer, which is only available
    // in the full boot path. In runOnePollCycle (test seam), we skip submission.

title: Discovered vaults never receive baseCoinType/quoteCoinType so trigger evaluation skips them
description: parseVaultCreatedEvent constructs a KnownVault with no baseCoinType / quoteCoinType (those are declared optional on the interface). The discovery path in index.ts inserts the parsed vault directly via registry.addOrUpdate. The trigger loop then guards with 'if (!vault.baseCoinType || !vault.quoteCoinType) continue;' (index.ts:158) — meaning every discovered vault is silently skipped during trigger evaluation, regardless of price. There is no module that resolves a vault's pool_id against the manifest to populate these fields.
impact: End-to-end keeper-detects-and-fires path is dead even if trigger submission were wired. The contract explicitly required a src/manifest.ts that resolves vault pool_id to (baseCoinType, quoteCoinType, baseDecimals, quoteDecimals, basePriceInfoObjectId, quotePriceInfoObjectId); that module is absent.
recommendation: Introduce src/manifest.ts as required by contract; in index.ts after parseVaultCreatedEvent and before addOrUpdate, look up the manifest pool entry by vault.pool_id and inject the resolved coin types and decimals into the KnownVault. Make baseCoinType/quoteCoinType non-optional on the discovery-side type so the gap surfaces as a type error.

title: Pool-to-oracle and pool-to-decimals mapping is hardcoded, defeating manifest abstraction
description: The price-loop hardcodes 'use DEEP oracle for base and SUI oracle for quote' and quoteDecimals: 9 with comments 'Default SUI decimals; manifest-driven in production' and 'Full manifest-driven mapping is handled in the manifest module'. Neither is true: there is no manifest module, and runOnePollCycle IS the production path. A SUI/USDC pool would silently use the wrong quote decimals (USDC = 6) and the wrong oracle pair. This is the same coupling failure as R2-002 (no abstraction layer between vault.pool_id and oracle pair).
impact: Multi-pool support advertised by the contract (DEEP/SUI and SUI/USDC, per manifest pools[]) does not work. Any vault on a non-DEEP/SUI pool computes a wildly wrong current_price and either fails to fire or fires with a price the on-chain assertion will reject.
recommendation: Introduce a manifest module with a function resolvePool(poolId) -> { baseCoinType, quoteCoinType, baseDecimals, quoteDecimals, basePriceInfoObjectId, quotePriceInfoObjectId }. The trigger loop iterates vaults, calls this resolver, then reads only the two oracles for that pool and applies the formula with the correct quoteDecimals.
evidence:
// For now, use DEEP oracle for base and SUI oracle for quote on the DEEP/SUI pool.
  // Full manifest-driven mapping is handled in the manifest module.

title: Contract-mandated src/manifest.ts module is missing
description: The contract's 'In scope' section lists src/manifest.ts as the manifest loader / pool resolver, alongside config.ts, pythReader.ts, etc. The implementer's actual module decomposition skips it; manifest typing is inlined in index.ts (SandboxManifest interface), and pool-resolution logic does not exist. This is the architectural seam the contract specifically called for to keep index.ts free of manifest knowledge.
impact: index.ts conflates wiring, manifest schema, pool resolution, and main loop, making it harder to test and harder to extend (new pools cannot be added without changing the entry-point file). The implementer's note that the layout 'MAY be collapsed or split differently provided each AC is satisfied' is stretched here because the satisfaction itself requires the resolver (see R2-002, R2-003).
recommendation: Extract SandboxManifest type, JSON loader, and a resolvePool/resolveOracles helper into src/manifest.ts. Keep index.ts focused on lifecycle + loop scheduling.

title: On-startup triggered-flag re-seed is implemented but never called
description: VaultRegistry.seedTriggeredFromChain is a documented contract decision (#3 — the keeper SHOULD re-read each known vault's on-chain triggered flag at startup before entering the trigger loop). The method exists and has unit tests, but main() never calls it. After a keeper restart immediately following a fire, the keeper would attempt a doomed-to-abort execute_trigger retry exactly as the contract warns.
impact: Restart correctness is broken. A keeper restarted between a fire and the operator inspecting state would log trigger_failed (EVaultTriggered) on the next price tick rather than no-op. Contract decision #3 explicitly calls this out as the keeper's responsibility.
recommendation: After the discovery loop's first tick (or a synchronous initial discovery call) in main(), iterate registry and call seedTriggeredFromChain(id, getObject) for each known vault before scheduling the price loop.

title: discoverVaultsTick params order does not match suix_queryEvents JSON-RPC signature
description: The Sui suix_queryEvents JSON-RPC signature is [query, cursor, limit, descending_order]. The keeper builds params as [{ MoveModule: ... }, { descending: false, limit: 50 }, cursor?]. The second element is shaped like SDK options rather than the raw cursor argument the JSON-RPC method expects, and cursor (when present) is appended in third position. This is a coupling/abstraction confusion between the high-level SDK call shape and the low-level JSON-RPC raw-fetch shape. The networkShape.test.ts mock returns canned data regardless of params shape, so the bug never surfaces in tests.
impact: Cursor-tracked discovery is non-functional against a real sandbox. Either the RPC will reject the call or it will silently ignore cursor, causing the keeper to re-process all events every poll (re-emit duplicate vault_discovered lines once dedup is bypassed by an envelope-shape change). The 'cursor is tracked per loop tick' AC3.8 verification language fails.
recommendation: Send raw JSON-RPC params as [query, cursor_or_null, limit, descending_bool]. Or, switch to the SDK's client.queryEvents which handles the parameter mapping. Add a test that asserts the second positional param equals the cursor (or null) rather than an options object.

title: Logger emitter signatures use type-erasing 'as unknown as Record' cast that defeats safety
description: Every emitter except logKeeperStarted forwards its args object via 'args as unknown as Record<string, unknown>'. The function emit() then iterates Object.entries and skips SECRET_KEYS — so secret-redaction does work for ad-hoc keys, but the type system stops giving any guarantee that the documented AC3.11 minimum field set is present. logKeeperStarted destructures explicitly (good); the others do not. This is a design inconsistency: either ALL emitters destructure to enforce field presence at the boundary, or all emitters accept an open record and rely on runtime defense alone.
impact: A future caller who mistakenly passes { vault_id, owner, pool_id, side } (no tp_price/sl_price) to logVaultDiscovered passes type-checking (the interface declares all fields required) but if a refactor relaxes the interface signature, the cast will silently swallow missing fields. Lower-impact than R2-001 through R2-006 because today's call sites are correct, but the pattern is fragile.
recommendation: Either (a) destructure each emitter's known fields exactly as logKeeperStarted does and pass that explicit object to emit(), removing the cast; or (b) drop the per-event TypeScript interface and accept Record<string, unknown> + a runtime schema validator. Pick one direction and apply uniformly.
evidence: emit('info', 'vault_discovered', args as unknown as Record<string, unknown>);

title: Two parallel logging surfaces: logger.ts to stdout vs vaultRegistry console.warn to stderr
description: VaultRegistry.seedTriggeredFromChain writes structured JSON via console.warn (which goes to stderr), inventing its own event name 'seed_triggered_warning' that is not part of the AC3.11 catalog. Meanwhile logger.ts is the documented stdout JSON channel. Operators / the Cycle 5 test harness subscribed to keeper stdout will not see these warnings; subscribers parsing stderr will receive a JSON shape (ts/level/event) that mimics but is not registered with the logger.
impact: Logging surface fragmentation. Two file boundaries can emit JSON-shaped operator-visible events; the contract was clear that 'Log lines go to stdout unconditionally'. The 'seed_triggered_warning' event is invisible to anything tailing stdout. Also makes secret redaction inconsistent — vaultRegistry bypasses logger.ts's SECRET_KEYS guard.
recommendation: Inject a logger callback into VaultRegistry (or import logger directly) and route the seed warning through a new logger emitter, e.g. logSeedTriggeredWarning. Decide once whether this event is part of the keeper's public log catalog and either add it to AC3.11 follow-up or downgrade to a debug-only channel.
evidence:
console.warn(
        JSON.stringify({
          ts: new Date().toISOString(),
          level: 'warn',
          event: 'seed_triggered_warning',

title: runOnePollCycle accepts pollIntervalMs and deepCoinId args it never uses
description: PollCycleArgs declares pollIntervalMs and deepCoinId as required fields. The function destructures them but never references them in the body (deepCoinId is only meaningful inside trigger submission — which doesn't happen, see R2-001; pollIntervalMs is the loop scheduler's concern, not a per-tick input). These dead args force every caller (including T-009 test) to pass placeholder values that mean nothing.
impact: Misleads readers about the function's contract; would surface as a real coupling problem if R2-001 is fixed and trigger submission is added — at which point only deepCoinId becomes meaningful (pollIntervalMs still belongs to the scheduler, not the tick).
recommendation: Drop pollIntervalMs from PollCycleArgs entirely. Pass deepCoinId only when (and if) the same function is generalized to also submit triggers; otherwise also drop it from the read-only path.

title: KEEPER_LOG_LEVEL config field is read but never consulted by logger
description: config.ts parses KEEPER_LOG_LEVEL into Config.logLevel; the contract states it 'gates additional debug events'. logger.ts has no level-gating at all — every emit() unconditionally writes to stdout. There is no concept of debug events to gate. The config field is therefore inert state.
impact: Operator expectation set by the config knob does not match runtime behavior. Either the knob should be removed, or debug-tier events should be added and gated behind it. As-is, an operator setting KEEPER_LOG_LEVEL=warn will still receive every info-level event.
recommendation: Either (a) remove logLevel from Config until a debug event surface lands, or (b) thread a logger factory createLogger(level: string) through the boot path that gates emit() against the configured level.

title: Boot path lacks faucet funding step required by contract
description: Contract Behavior step 3 mandates: 'requests gas from the localnet faucet at network.faucetUrl if its balance is insufficient to fund a single execute_trigger call; failure to fund halts the boot with a clear error.' main() generates the keypair, logs keeper_started, and immediately enters the loop. There is no balance check, no faucet request, no halt-on-fund-fail. The implementer's manifest type even has faucetUrl typed as optional, signaling the intent was abandoned.
impact: Even if R2-001 (trigger wiring) is fixed, the first execute_trigger submission will fail with insufficient gas. The keeper will log trigger_failed in a tight loop until an operator manually funds the address, with no actionable boot-time message.
recommendation: Insert a getBalance + faucet POST step between the keypair generation and the loop. On failure, throw with a message identifying network.faucetUrl and the keeper address. Add an integration test against the canned fetch spy similar to T-009 to lock the call shape.

title: tx.build is called with 'undefined as never' client cast that masks unsafe call
description: signAndSubmitTrigger calls 'tx.build({ client: undefined as never })' to avoid the SDK's normal client dependency. SDK 2.x Transaction.build requires a client to resolve unresolved object refs (initial shared versions) for any tx.object(id) input. The trigger PTB references vault, pool, deep-coin-source, and clock — at minimum vault and pool are shared and must be resolved. Casting to 'never' silences TypeScript but does not change runtime: the build call will throw at first unresolved input.
impact: If R2-001 is fixed and signAndSubmitTrigger is invoked at runtime, the build step fails for any shared-object reference. The cast advertises 'we know better than the type system' but production behavior contradicts that.
recommendation: Either (a) accept a real SuiJsonRpcClient (or the underlying ObjectCache abstraction) into SignAndSubmitArgs and pass it to tx.build; or (b) explicitly set every shared object reference via tx.sharedObjectRef({ objectId, mutable, initialSharedVersion }) after looking versions up via raw fetch — but then the cast is no longer needed and you can pass {} as the build options. The 'as never' is the design smell.
evidence: const txBytes = await tx.build({ client: undefined as never });

title: Dead 'void rpcUrl' suppresses unused warning for a const that exists only to mask a missing wire
description: main() declares 'const rpcUrl = manifest.network.rpcUrl;' on line 301 then never uses it directly; line 343 has 'void rpcUrl; // suppress unused warning — used by runOnePollCycle via manifest'. The const + suppression pattern is a code smell — the const is genuinely dead, since runOnePollCycle reads the rpcUrl from manifest.network.rpcUrl itself. The comment justifying it is incorrect.
impact: Cosmetic; flags the same wiring incoherence captured in R2-001 (main() lacks the missing pieces). Clean up signals.
recommendation: Delete the const and the 'void rpcUrl' line.
evidence: void rpcUrl; // suppress unused warning — used by runOnePollCycle via manifest

title: Two competing parsing paths: SandboxManifest.pools typed as Record but contract uses array
description: Contract Behavior step 1 references 'pools[]' (an array indexed by integer position) used to map vault pool_id to coin types. SandboxManifest in index.ts types pools as 'Record<string, { ... }>' (keyed by pool name). The networkShape test fixture uses { DEEP_SUI: { ... } }. Either is workable, but the type drift between contract wording and code, combined with the absence of any pool-resolution function (R2-002, R2-003, R2-004), makes the field shape untestable end-to-end. Whichever shape the live sandbox manifest uses is not captured anywhere in code.
impact: When the manifest module lands (R2-004) the type may need to change, breaking the existing test fixture. Worth picking a canonical shape now and asserting against the live localnet.json.
recommendation: Read ~/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/deployments/localnet.json shape during the design pass and pin SandboxManifest.pools to whatever the live sandbox emits. Add a JSON fixture under tests/fixtures/ captured from the live sandbox so the type and the runtime stay in sync.

title: Network-shape lockdown (T-009) is a real architectural commitment but bypassed by production main path
description: T-009 is genuine — the keeper's runOnePollCycle uses raw fetch JSON-RPC against manifest.network.rpcUrl and never imports any DeepBook helper SDK. The architectural commitment to 'no @mysten/deepbook-v3' is solid in package.json. However, because main() reuses the test seam unchanged (R2-001), a future maintainer who adds trigger submission to main() may import additional client surface (e.g. SuiJsonRpcClient) without re-running T-009 against the new main path. The lockdown locks down the test seam, not the production loop. This is the Cycle 1 lesson half-applied.
impact: If trigger-submission code is added to main() with a real client, T-009 will continue to pass against runOnePollCycle while production may invoke unforeseen routes (e.g. an SDK helper that pulls /faucet/v2/gas, /metrics, etc). The lockdown's safety claim is only as strong as the path it covers.
recommendation: Extract the production main loop body into a runMainTick(args, signer, signAndSubmit) function and have the network-shape test exercise it with a no-op signer. The function-under-test for T-009 should be the same code path production runs.
evidence:
// Outbound HTTP:
 *   - suix_queryEvents (vault discovery) → rpcUrl
 *   - sui_getObject + sui_devInspectTransactionBlock (price reads) → rpcUrl
 *
 * Never calls DeepBook indexer routes (AC3.7 — no @mysten/deepbook-v3 dep).

title: Per-vault iteration in trigger loop has no concurrency guard against double-fire across ticks
description: The trigger loop iterates registry.iterate() and (once R2-001 is fixed) would await signAndSubmitTrigger per vault. Because the main loop awaits runOnePollCycle and only then schedules the next tick, intra-tick double-fire is prevented by sequential iteration plus registry.markTriggered. However, there is no in-flight guard: if a tick takes longer than pollIntervalMs (e.g. RPC slowdown), Node's setTimeout will fire on schedule but await ordering serializes them — fine for correctness, but the contract permits parallel submission. If the implementer later adds Promise.all for parallelism, two ticks can race against the same vault before markTriggered lands. Worth flagging as a future-design hazard rather than a current bug.
impact: Today: no observable issue (sequential awaits). After parallel submission lands: possible double-fire of execute_trigger, second one aborts EVaultTriggered, logs trigger_failed, recoverable but noisy.
recommendation: Add an inFlight: Set<string> on VaultRegistry. Before submission, registry.beginFire(vaultId) — returns false if already in-flight. After submission completes (success or failure), registry.endFire(vaultId). markTriggered is set on success only.
